price_basis: split-adjusted, NOT dividend-adjusted (NU pays no dividend, so both bases agree). Regular session bars.
time_convention: Every date is an exchange trading date (America/New_York) and names the 1D bar of that session, never an intraday moment. Put the point on the bar whose date on the TradingView time axis equals this date; if the tool needs a timestamp, read it from that bar, do not build it from local midnight. After drawing, read each object back and confirm its bar date. 2026-11-13, 2026-11-16, 2026-12-21 and 2027-03-31 are trading days at or after the last bar in the data (12.11.2026); on 13.11 the bar may still be forming.
data_alignment_source: runs/tickers/NU_2026-11-13/ta/data/NU_daily.csv (Yahoo consolidated daily bars), read by build_package.py
tolerance_note: The numbers here come from consolidated daily bars; TradingView can show one exchange, so highs and lows can differ by a cent. At NU's price a cent is about 0.1%: a 0.25% high/low tolerance is about 3 cents. A Fibonacci anchor that differs by a cent moves its levels by about a cent: that is fine.

direct.fib_convention: TradingView level price = point_2 + level x (point_1 - point_2), so level 0 sits at point_2 and level 1 at point_1. FIB-decline: point 1 (first click) = the HIGH 18.98 (29.1.2026), point 2 = the LOW 11.20 (3.6.2026): 0 at 11.20, 0.236 at 13.04. FIB-advance: point 1 = the LOW 3.26 (25.5.2022), point 2 = the HIGH 18.98 (29.1.2026): 0 at 18.98, 0.382 at 12.97, 0.5 at 11.12. If a test level is at the wrong end, the points are reversed: swap them or tick 'Reverse'. Show only 0, 0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.786, 1; switch off all other levels, the background fill and 'extend lines left'. Check each drawn level against the listed price (tolerance in 'tolerance').

rules_for_the_drawing_session: Draw only what this file lists, with these prices. Do not add trend lines, patterns, targets or stops.
This is a research map, not a trade plan. It contains no order, alert, position size or stop. Do not create orders or alerts from it.

Name every drawing (rectangle, horizontal line, text, vertical line, Fibonacci, anchored VWAP) object_prefix + id, e.g. NU-1113-R-1300. The name is the object-tree name, not the visible label. Indicators are not renamed. If the tool cannot set names, write a list of id -> TradingView object id in the session report so a later package can remove the set.
If a data_alignment_check is outside its tolerance, stop and report: the chart is on a different price basis.
